$\mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { C S , n b } }$ is the non-balanced charge-sustaining fuel consumption of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test, not corrected for the energy balance, according to Table A8/7, step no. 1, $\mathrm { k g / 1 0 0 \ k m }$ .

4.2.1.2.3. If the correction of the fuel consumption is required according to paragraph 1.1.3. of Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex or in the case that the correction according to paragraph 1.1.4. of Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex was applied, the fuel consumption correction coefficient shall be determined according to paragraph 2. of Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex. The corrected charge-sustaining fuel consumption shall be determined using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { F C _ { C S } = F C _ { C S , n b } - K _ { f u e l , F C H V } \times E C _ { D C , C S } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { C S } }$ is the charge-sustaining fuel consumption of the chargesustaining Type 1 test according to Table A8/7, step no. $\gtrsim , \ k g / 1 0 0 \ k m$ ;

FCCS,nb is the non-balanced fuel consumption of the chargesustaining Type 1 test, not corrected for the energy balance, according to Table A8/7, step no. 1, $\mathrm { k g / 1 0 0 \ k m }$ ;

ECDC,CS is the electric energy consumption of the chargesustaining Type 1 test according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

Kfuel,FCHV is the fuel consumption correction coefficient according to paragraph 2.3.1. of Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex, $( \mathrm { k g / 1 0 0 \ k m } ) / ( \mathrm { W h / k m } )$ .

4.2.2.

Utility factor-weighted charge-depleting fuel consumption for OVCHEVs

The utility factor-weighted charge-depleting fuel consumption $\mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { C D } }$ shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { F C _ { C D } = \frac { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } ( U F _ { j } \times F C _ { C D , j } ) } { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } U F _ { j } } }
$$

where:

FCCD is the utility factor weighted charge-depleting fuel consumption, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
FCCD,j is the fuel consumption for phase j of the chargedepleting Type 1 test, determined according to paragraph 6. of Sub-Annex 7, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
UFj is the utility factor of phase j according to Appendix 5 of this Sub-Annex;   
j is the index number of the phase considered;   
k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle according to paragraph 3.2.4.4 of this Sub-Annex.

In the case that the interpolation method is applied, k shall be the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle of vehicle $\mathrm { ~ L ~ n _ { v e h \_ L } }$ .

If the transition cycle number driven by vehicle H, $\mathrm { n _ { v e h _ { H } } }$ , and, if applicable, by an individual vehicle within the vehicle interpolation family, $\mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h i n d } }$ , is lower than the transition cycle number driven by vehicle $\mathrm { ~ L ~ } ~ \mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h \ L } }$ the confirmation cycle of vehicle $\mathrm { H }$ and, if applicable, an individual vehicle shall be included in the calculation. The fuel consumption of each phase of the confirmation cycle shall be calculated in accordance with paragraph 6. of Sub-Annex 7 with the criteria emission over the complete confirmation cycle and the applicable $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ phase value which shall be corrected to an electric energy consumption of zero, $\mathrm { E C _ { D C , C D , j } = 0 }$ , by using the $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass correction coefficient $\left( \mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 } } \right)$ in accordance with Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex.

# 4.2.3.

Utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted fuel consumption from the chargedepleting and charge-sustaining Type 1 test shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { F C _ { w e i g h t e d } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } ( U F _ { j } \times F C _ { C D , j } ) + ( 1 - \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } U F _ { j } ) \times F C _ { C S } }
$$

where:

FCweighted is the utility factor-weighted fuel consumption, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
$\mathrm { U F _ { j } }$ is the utility factor of phase j according to Appendix 5 of this Sub-Annex;   
FCCD,j is the fuel consumption of phase $\mathrm { j }$ of the chargedepleting Type 1 test, determined according to paragraph 6. of Sub-Annex 7, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
FCCS is the fuel consumption determined according to Table A8/6, step no. 1, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
j is the index number of the phase considered;   
k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle according to paragraph 3.2.4.4. of this Sub-Annex.

In the case that the interpolation method is applied, $\mathrm { k }$ shall be the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle of vehicle L $\mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h \_ L } }$ .

If the transition cycle number driven by vehicle H, $\boldsymbol { \mathrm { n } } _ { \mathrm { v e h _ { H } } }$ , and, if applicable, by an individual vehicle within the vehicle interpolation family $\mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h } _ { \mathrm { i n d } } }$ is lower than the transition cycle number driven by vehicle L, $\mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h \_ L } }$ , the confirmation cycle of vehicle H and, if applicable, an individual vehicle shall be included in the calculation.

The fuel consumption of each phase of the confirmation cycle shall be calculated in accordance with paragraph 6. of Sub-Annex 7 with the criteria emission over the complete confirmation cycle and the applicable $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ phase value which shall be corrected to an electric energy consumption of zero $\mathrm { E C _ { D C , C D , j } = 0 }$ by using the $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass correction coefficient $\left( \mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 } } \right)$ in accordance with Appendix 2 to this Sub-Annex.

4.3.

# Calculation of electric energy consumption

For the determination of the electric energy consumption based on the current and voltage determined according to Appendix 3 of this Sub-Annex, the following equations shall be used:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , j } = \frac { \Delta E _ { R E E S S , j } } { d _ { j } } }
$$

where:

ECDC,j is the electric energy consumption over the considered period $\mathrm { j }$ based on the REESS depletion, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
ΔEREESS,j is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the considered period j, Wh;   
dj is the distance driven in the considered period $\mathrm { j , ~ k m }$ ;

and

$$
\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , j } } = \sum _ { \mathrm { j = 1 } } ^ { \mathrm { n } } \Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , j , i } }
$$

where:

ΔEREESS,j,i: is the electric energy change of REESS i during the considered period $\mathrm { j } , \mathrm { W h }$ ;

and

$$
\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { j } , \mathrm { i } } = \frac { 1 } { 3 6 0 0 } \times \int _ { \mathrm { t _ { \mathrm { 0 } } } } ^ { \mathrm { t _ { \mathrm { e n d } } } } \mathrm { U ( t ) } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { j } , \mathrm { i } } \times \mathrm { I ( t ) } _ { \mathrm { j } , \mathrm { i } } \mathrm { d t }
$$

where:

U(t)REESS,j,i is the voltage of REESS i during the considered period j determined according to Appendix 3 to this SubAnnex, V;   
t0 is the time at the beginning of the considered period j, s;   
tend is the time at the end of the considered period j, s;   
$\mathrm { I ( t ) _ { j , i } }$ is the electric current of REESS i during the considered period j determined according to Appendix 3 to this Sub-Annex, A;

▼B

i is the index number of the considered REESS;   
n is the total number of REESS;   
j is the index for the considered period, where a period can be any combination of phases or cycles;   
1 3600 is the conversion factor from Ws to Wh.

4.3.1.

Utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for OVCHEVs

The utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { A C , C D } = \frac { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } ( \mathrm { U F _ { j } \times E C _ { A C , C D , j } ) } } { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } \mathrm { U F _ { j } } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { A C , C D } }$ is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains, Wh/km;   
$\mathrm { U F _ { j } }$ is the utility factor of phase $\mathrm { j }$ in accordance with Appendix 5 to this Sub-Annex;   
ECAC,CD,j is the electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains of phase j, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { A C , C D , j } = \mathrm { E C _ { D C , C D , j } \times \frac { E _ { A C } } { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } \Delta \Delta \Delta \mathrm { E _ { R E E S S , j } } } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { D C , C D , j } }$ is the electric energy consumption based on the REESS depletion of phase j of the charge-depleting Test 1 in accordance with paragraph 4.3. of this SubAnnex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
$\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { A C } }$ is the recharged electric energy from the mains determined in accordance with paragraph 3.2.4.6. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;   
ΔEREESS,j is the electric energy change of all REESSs of phase j in accordance with paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;   
j is the index number for the considered phase;   
k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle in accordance with paragraph 3.2.4.4. of this Sub-Annex. In the case that the interpolation method is applied, k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle of L, $\mathrm { n } _ { \mathrm { v e h \_ L } }$ .

Utility factor-weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { A C , w e i g h t e d } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } ( U F _ { j } \times E C _ { A C , C D , j } ) }
$$

where:

ECAC,weighted is the utility factor-weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains, Wh/km;   
UFj is the utility factor of phase j according to Appendix 5 of this Sub-Annex;   
ECAC,CD,j is the electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains of phase j according to paragraph 4.3.1. of this Sub-Annex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
j is the index number of the phase considered;   
k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle in accordance with paragraph 3.2.4.4. of this Sub-Annex. in the case that the interpolation method is applied, k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle of vehicle L, nveh_L.

Electric energy consumption for OVC-HEVs

# 4.3.3.1.

Determination of cycle-specific electric energy consumption

The electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the equivalent all-electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C } = { \frac { \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { A C } } } { \mathrm { E A E R } } }
$$

where:

EC is the electric energy consumption of the applicable WLTP test cycle based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the equivalent all-electric range, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
EAC is the recharged electric energy from the mains according to paragraph 3.2.4.6. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;   
EAER is the equivalent all-electric range according to paragraph 4.4.4.1. of this Sub-Annex, km.

4.3.3.2. Determination of phase-specific electric energy consumption

The phase-specific electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the phase-specific equivalent all-electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { p } = \frac { E _ { A C } } { E A E R _ { p } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { P } }$ : is the phase-specific electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the equivalent all-electric range, Wh/km;

$\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { A C } }$ : is the recharged electric energy from the mains according to paragraph 3.2.4.6. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

$\mathrm { E A E R _ { P } }$ : is the phase-specific equivalent all-electric range according to paragraph 4.4.4.2. of this Sub-Annex, km.

4.3.4. Electric energy consumption of PEVs

4.3.4.1.

The electric energy consumption determined in this paragraph shall be calculated only if the vehicle was able to follow the applicable test cycle within the speed trace tolerances in accordance with paragraph 2.6.8.3. of Sub-Annex 6 during the entire considered period.

# 4.3.4.2.

Electric energy consumption determination of the applicable WLTP test cycle

The electric energy consumption of the applicable WLTP test cycle based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the pure electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { W L T C } } = { \frac { \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { A C } } } { \mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { W L T C } } } }
$$

where:

ECWLTC

is the electric energy consumption of the applicable WLTP test cycle based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the pure electric range for the applicable WLTP test cycle, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

EAC

is the recharged electric energy from the mains according to paragraph 3.4.4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

is the pure electric range for the applicable WLTP test cycle as calculated according to paragraph 4.4.2.1.1. or paragraph 4.4.2.2.1. of this Sub-Annex, depending on the PEV test procedure that must be used, km.

4.3.4.3.

Electric energy consumption determination of the applicable WLTP city test cycle

The electric energy consumption of the applicable WLTP city test cycle based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the pure electric range for the applicable WLTP city test cycle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { \mathrm { { c i t y } } } = \frac { E _ { \mathrm { { A C } } } } { P E R _ { \mathrm { { c i t y } } } } }
$$

where:

ECcity is the electric energy consumption of the applicable WLTP city test cycle based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the pure electric range for the applicable WLTP city test cycle, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

$\mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { A C } }$ is the recharged electric energy from the mains according to paragraph 3.4.4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

$\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$ is the pure electric range for the applicable WLTP city test cycle as calculated according to paragraph 4.4.2.1.2. or paragraph 4.4.2.2.2. of this Sub-Annex, depending on the PEV test procedure that must be used, km.

# 4.3.4.4.

Electric energy consumption determination of the phase-specific values

The electric energy consumption of each individual phase based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the phase-specific pure electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { p } = \frac { E _ { A C } } { P E R _ { p } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { \mathrm { p } } }$ is the electric energy consumption of each individual phase $\mathfrak { p }$ based on the recharged electric energy from the mains and the phase-specific pure electric range, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$

EAC is the recharged electric energy from the mains according to paragraph 3.4.4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

PERp is the phase-specific pure electric range as calculated according to paragraph 4.4.2.1.3. or paragraph 4.4.2.2.3. of this Sub-Annex, depending on the PEV test procedure used, km.

4.4. Calculation of electric ranges

4.4.1.

All-electric ranges AER and $\mathrm { \Delta A E R _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } }$ for OVC-HEVs .1. All-electric range AER

The all-electric range AER for OVC-HEVs shall be determined from the charge-depleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 1 test sequence and is referenced in paragraph 3.2.6.1. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 3 test sequence by driving the applicable WLTP test cycle according to paragraph 1.4.2.1. of this Sub-Annex. The AER is defined as the distance driven from the beginning of the charge-depleting Type 1 test to the point in time where the combustion engine starts consuming fuel.

# 4.4.1.2. All-electric range city $\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$

4.4.1.2.1. The all-electric range city $\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$ for OVC-HEVs shall be determined from the charge-depleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 1 test sequence and is referenced in paragraph 3.2.6.1. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 3 test sequence by driving the applicable WLTP city test cycle according to paragraph 1.4.2.2. of this SubAnnex. The $\mathrm { \Delta A E R _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } }$ is defined as the distance driven from the beginning of the charge-depleting Type 1 test to the point in time where the combustion engine starts consuming fuel.

4.4.1.2.2. As an alternative to paragraph 4.4.1.2.1. of this Sub-Annex, the allelectric range city $\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$ may be determined from the chargedepleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this SubAnnex by driving the applicable WLTP test cycles according to paragraph 1.4.2.1. of this Sub-Annex. In that case, the chargedepleting Type 1 test by driving the applicable WLTP city test cycle shall be omitted and the all-electric range city $\mathrm { \Delta A E R _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } }$ shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } = \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C , c i t y } } }
$$

where:

UBEcity

is the usable REESS energy determined from the beginning of the charge-depleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex by driving applicable WLTP test cycles until the point in time where the combustion engine starts consuming fuel, Wh;

$\mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C } , \mathrm { c i t y } }$ is the weighted electric energy consumption of the pure electrically driven applicable WLTP city test cycles of the charge-depleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex by driving applicable WLTP test cycle(s), $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { U B E _ { c i t y } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k + 1 } \Delta E _ { R E E S S , j } }
$$

where:

<table><tr><td>△EREESS.j</td><td>is the electric energy change of all REESSs during phase j,Wh;</td></tr><tr><td>j</td><td>is the index number of the considered phase;</td></tr><tr><td>k+1</td><td>is the number of the phases driven from the beginning</td></tr></table>

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , c i t y } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { c i t y , p e } } E C _ { D C , c i t y , j } \times K _ { c i t y , j } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { D C , c i t y , j } }$ is the electric energy consumption for the jth pure electrically driven WLTP city test cycle of the chargedepleting Type 1 test according to paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex by driving applicable WLTP test cycles, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
Kcity,j is the weighting factor for the jth pure electrically driven applicable WLTP city test cycle of the chargedepleting Type 1 test according to paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex by driving applicable WLTP test cycles;   
j is the index number of the pure electrically driven applicable WLTP city test cycle considered;   
ncity,pe is the number of pure electrically driven applicable WLTP city test cycles;

and

$$
\mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { c i t y , l } } = \frac { \Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , c i t y , l } } } { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } }
$$

where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , c i t y , 1 } }$ is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, Wh;

and

$$
\mathrm { K _ { c i t y , j } = \frac { 1 - K _ { c i t y , l } } { n _ { c i t y , p e } - 1 } f o r j = 2 \ t o \ n _ { c i t y , p e } . }
$$

4.4.2. Pure electric range for PEVs

The ranges determined in this paragraph shall only be calculated if the vehicle was able to follow the applicable WLTP test cycle within the speed trace tolerances in accordance with paragraph 2.6.8.3. of Sub-Annex 6 during the entire considered period.

Determination of the pure electric ranges when the shortened Type 1 test procedure is applied

4.4.2.1.1. The pure -electric range for the applicable WLTP test cycle PERWLTC for PEVs shall be calculated from the shortened Type 1 test as described in paragraph 3.4.4.2. of this Sub-Annex using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { W L T C } } = { \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C } , \mathrm { W L T C } } } }
$$

where:

UBESTP

is the usable REESS energy determined from the beginning of the shortened Type 1 test procedure until the break-off criterion as defined in paragraph 3.4.4.2.3. of this Sub-Annex is reached, Wh;

ECDC,WLTC is the weighted electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ and $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure Type 1 test, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { U B E _ { S T P } = \Delta E _ { R E E S S , D S _ { 1 } } + \Delta E _ { R E E S S , D S _ { 2 } } + \Delta E _ { R E E S S , C S S _ { M } } + \Delta E _ { R E E S S , C C S _ { R } } }
$$

where:

ΔEREESS;DS1 is the electric energy change of all REESSs during $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;   
ΔEREESS;DS2 is the electric energy change of all REESSs during $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;   
ΔEREESS;CSSM is the electric energy change of all REESSs during $\mathrm { C S } \mathrm { S } _ { \mathrm { M } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;   
ΔEREESS;CSSE is the electric energy change of all REESSs during $\mathrm { C S S _ { E } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , W L T C } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { 2 } E C _ { D C , W L T C , j } \times K _ { W L T C , j } }
$$

where:

ECDC,WLTC,j is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP test cycle of $\mathrm { D S _ { j } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this SubAnnex, Wh/km;   
kWLTC,j is the weighting factor for the applicable WLTP test cycle of $\mathrm { D S _ { j } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure;

and

$$
{ \mathrm { K } } _ { \mathrm { W L T C , 1 } } = { \frac { \Delta { \mathrm { E } } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , W L T C , 1 } } } { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } } { \mathrm { a n d ~ K } } _ { \mathrm { W L T C , 2 } } = 1 - { \mathrm { K } } _ { \mathrm { W L T C , 1 } }
$$

where:

KWLTC,j

is the weighting factor for the applicable WLTP test cycle of $\mathrm { D S _ { j } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure;

ΔEREESS,WLTC,1 is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the applicable WLTP test cycle from $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;

# 4.4.2.1.2.

The pure electric range for the applicable WLTP city test cycle $\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$ for PEVs shall be calculated from the shortened Type 1 test procedure as described in paragraph 3.4.4.2. of this SubAnnex using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } = \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C , c i t y } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } }$ is the usable REESS energy according to paragraph 4.4.2.1.1. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

ECDC,city is the weighted electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ and $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , c i t y } = \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { 4 } E C _ { D C , c i t y , j } \times K _ { c i t y , j } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { D C , c i t y , j } }$ is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP city test cycle where the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 1$ , the second applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j }$ $= 2$ , the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 3$ and the second applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 4$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

Kcity,j is the weighting factor for the applicable WLTP city test cycle where the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 1$ , the second applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as ${ \mathrm { j } } = 2$ , the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as ${ \mathrm { j } } = 3$ and the second applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 4$ ,

and

$$
\mathrm { K _ { c i t y , l } = \frac { \Delta E _ { R E E S S , c i t y , l } } { U B E _ { S T P } } a n d ~ K _ { c i t y , j } = \frac { 1 - K _ { c i t y , l } } { 3 } f o r ~ j = 2 ~ . . . ~ 4 }
$$

where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , c i t y , 1 } }$ is the energy change of all REESSs during the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh;

4.4.2.1.3. The phase-specific pure electric-range $\mathrm { P E R _ { p } }$ for PEVs shall be calculated from the Type 1 test as described in paragraph 3.4.4.2. of this Sub-Annex by using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { p } } = \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C , p } } }
$$

where:

UBESTP

is the usable REESS energy in accordance with paragraph 4.4.2.1.1. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

ECDC,p

is the weighted electric energy consumption for each individual phase of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ and $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

In the case that phase $\boldsymbol { \mathrm { p } } = \mathrm { l o w }$ and phase ${ \mathfrak { p } } =$ medium, the following equations shall be used:

$$
\begin{array} { r } { \mathrm { E C _ { D C , p } } = \sum _ { \mathrm { j = 1 } } ^ { 4 } \mathrm { E C _ { D C , p , j } } \times \mathrm { K _ { p , j } } } \end{array}
$$

where:

ECDC,p,j

is the electric energy consumption for phase $\mathfrak { p }$ where the first phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { ~ j ~ } = \mathrm { ~ 1 ~ }$ , the second phase p of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as ${ \mathrm { j } } = 2$ , the first phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 3$ and the second phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 4$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

$\mathrm { K _ { p , j } }$

is the weighting factor for phase $\mathfrak { p }$ where the first phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { ~ j ~ } = \ 1$ , the second phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ is indicated as ${ \mathrm { j } } = 2$ , the first phase p of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as ${ \mathrm { j } } = 3$ , and the second phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 2 }$ is indicated as $\mathrm { j } = 4$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure;

and

$$
{ \bf K } _ { \mathrm { p , 1 } } = \frac { \Delta { \mathrm { E } } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , p , 1 } } } { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } \mathrm { a n d } \mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { p , j } } = \frac { 1 - { \mathrm { K } } _ { \mathrm { p , l } } } { 3 } \mathrm { f o r } \mathrm { j } = 2 \dots 4
$$

where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { p } , 1 }$ : is the energy change of all REESSs during the first phase p of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh.

In the case that phase $\mathrm { \tt ~ p ~ } = \mathrm { \ h i g h }$ and phase ${ \mathfrak { p } } =$ extraHigh, the following equations shall be used:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , p } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { 2 } E C _ { D C , p , j } \times K _ { p , j } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { D C , p , j } }$ is the electric energy consumption for phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S _ { j } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh/km;

$\mathrm { k _ { p , j } }$ is the weighting factor for phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S _ { j } }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure

and

$$
{ \bf K } _ { \mathrm { p , l } } = \frac { \Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , p , l } } } { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { S T P } } } \mathrm { a n d } \ { \bf K } _ { \mathrm { p , 2 } } = 1 - { \bf K } _ { \mathrm { p , l } }
$$

where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { p } , 1 }$ is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the first phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of $\mathrm { D S } _ { 1 }$ of the shortened Type 1 test procedure, Wh.

# 4.4.2.2.

Determination of the pure electric ranges when the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure is applied

4.4.2.2.1. The pure electric range for the applicable WLTP test cycle $\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { W L T P } }$ for PEVs shall be calculated from the Type 1 test as described in paragraph 3.4.4.1. of this Sub-Annex using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { W L T C } } = { \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C } , \mathrm { W L T C } } } }
$$

where:

UBECCP is the usable REESS energy determined from the beginning of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure until the break-off criterion according to paragraph 3.4.4.1.3. of this Sub-Annex is reached, Wh;

ECDC,WLTC

is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP test cycle determined from completely driven applicable WLTP test cycles of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { U B E _ { C C P } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } \Delta E _ { R E E S S , j } }
$$

where:

ΔEREESS,j is the electric energy change of all REESSs during phase j of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, Wh;

is the index number of the phase considered;

k is the number of phases driven from the beginning up to and including the phase where the break-off criterion is reached;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , W L T C } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { W L T C } } E C _ { D C , W L T C , j } \times K _ { W L T C , j } }
$$

where:

ECDC,WLTC,j is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP test cycle $\mathrm { j }$ of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this SubAnnex, Wh/km;   
KWLTC,j is the weighting factor for the applicable WLTP test cycle j of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure;   
j is the index number of the applicable WLTP test cycle;   
nWLTC is the whole number of complete applicable WLTP test cycles driven;

and

where:

ΔEREESS,WLTC,1 is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the first applicable WLTP test cycle of the consecutive Type 1 test cycle procedure, Wh.

4.4.2.2.2. The pure electric range for the WLTP city test cycle $\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } }$ for PEVs shall be calculated from the Type 1 test as described in paragraph 3.4.4.1. of this Sub-Annex using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { c i t y } } = \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C , c i t y } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } }$ is the usable REESS energy according to paragraph 4.4.2.2.1. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

ECDC,city is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP city test cycle determined from completely driven applicable WLTP city test cycles of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , c i t y } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { \mathrm { { c i t y } } } } E C _ { D C , c i t y , j \times } K _ { c i t y , j } }
$$

where:

ECDC,city,j is the electric energy consumption for the applicable WLTP city test cycle j of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this SubAnnex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
Kcity,j is the weighting factor for the applicable WLTP city test cycle j of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure;   
j is the index number of the applicable WLTP city test cycle;   
ncity is the whole number of complete applicable WLTP city test cycles driven;

and where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , c i t y , 1 } }$ is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the first applicable WLTP city test cycle of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, Wh.

4.4.2.2.3. The phase-specific pure electric-range $\mathrm { P E R _ { p } }$ for PEVs shall be calculated from the Type 1 test as described in paragraph 3.4.4.1. of this Sub-Annex using the following equations:

$$
\mathrm { P E R } _ { \mathrm { p } } = { \frac { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } } } { \mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { D C , p } } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } }$ is the usable REESS energy according to paragraph 4.4.2.2.1. of this Sub-Annex, Wh;

ECDC,p

is the electric energy consumption for the considered phase p determined from completely driven phases p of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

and

$$
\begin{array} { r } { \mathrm { E C _ { D C , p } } = \sum _ { \mathrm { j = 1 } } ^ { \textrm { n p } } \mathrm { E C _ { D C , p , j } } \times \mathrm { K _ { p , j } } } \end{array}
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C _ { D C , p , j } }$ is the jth electric energy consumption for the considered phase $\mathfrak { p }$ of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
$\mathrm { k _ { p , j } }$ is the jth weighting factor for the considered phase p of the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure;   
j is the index number of the considered phase p;   
$\mathfrak { n } _ { \mathfrak { p } }$ is the whole number of complete WLTC phases p driven;

and

$$
{ \mathrm { K } } _ { { \mathrm { p } } , 1 } = { \frac { \Delta { \mathrm { E } } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , p , l } } } { \mathrm { U B E } _ { \mathrm { C C P } } } } { \mathrm { a n d } } { \mathrm { K } } _ { { \mathrm { p } } , { \mathrm { j } } } = { \frac { 1 - { \mathrm { K } } _ { { \mathrm { p } } , 1 } } { { \mathrm { n } } _ { \mathrm { p } } - 1 } } { \mathrm { f o r ~ j } } = 2 \dots { \mathrm { n } } _ { \mathrm { p } }
$$

where:

$\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { p } , 1 }$ is the electric energy change of all REESSs during the first driven phase p during the consecutive cycle Type 1 test procedure, Wh.

4.4.3.

# Charge-depleting cycle range for OVC-HEVs

The charge-depleting cycle range $\mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D C } }$ shall be determined from the charge-depleting Type 1 test described in paragraph 3.2.4.3. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 1 test sequence and is referenced in paragraph 3.2.6.1. of this Sub-Annex as part of the Option 3 test sequence. The $\mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D C } }$ is the distance driven from the beginning of the charge-depleting Type 1 test to the end of the transition cycle according to paragraph 3.2.4.4 of this Sub-Annex.

# 4.4.4.

# Equivalent all-electric range for OVC-HEVs

# 4.4.4.1.

Determination of cycle-specific equivalent all-electric range

The cycle-specific equivalent all-electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E A E R } = \left( \frac { \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C S } } - \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C D , a v g } } } { \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C S } } } \right) \times \mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D C } }
$$

where:

EAER

is the cycle-specific equivalent all-electric range, km;

and

$$
\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 } , \mathrm { { C D } , \mathrm { { a v g } } } } } = \frac { \sum _ { \mathrm { { j = 1 } } } ^ { \mathrm { { k } } } ( \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 } , \mathrm { { C D } , \mathrm { { j } } } } } \times \mathbf { d } _ { \mathrm { { j } } } ) } { \sum _ { \mathrm { { j = 1 } } } ^ { \mathrm { { k } } } \mathbf { d } _ { \mathrm { { j } } } }
$$

where:

$\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 } , \mathrm { C D } , \mathrm { a v g } }$ is the arithmetic average charge-depleting $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission, $\mathrm { { g } / \mathrm { { k m } } }$ ;   
MCO2,CD,j is the $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission determined according to paragraph 3.2.1. of Sub-Annex 7 of phase $\mathrm { j }$ of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, $\mathrm { { g } / k m }$ ;   
dj is the distance driven in phase $\mathrm { j }$ of the chargedepleting Type 1 test, km;   
j is the index number of the considered phase;   
k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle n according to paragraph 3.2.4.4 of this Sub-Annex.

Determination of the phase-specific and city equivalent all-electric range

The phase-specific and city equivalent all-electric range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E A E R _ { p } = \left( \frac { M _ { C O _ { 2 } , C S , p } - M _ { C O _ { 2 } , C D , a v g , p } } { M _ { C O _ { 2 } , C S , p } } \right) \times \frac { \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { k } \Delta E _ { R E E S S , j } } { E C _ { D C , C D , p } } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E A E R _ { p } }$ is the equivalent all-electric range for the considered period p, km;   
$\mathrm { M _ { C O _ { 2 } , C S , p } }$ is the phase-specific $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission from the charge-sustaining Type 1 test for the considered period $\mathfrak { p }$ according to Table A8/5, step no. 7, g/km;   
ΔEREESS,j are the electric energy changes of all REESSs during the considered phase $\mathrm { j }$ , Wh;   
ECDC,CD,p is the electric energy consumption over the considered period p based on the REESS depletion, Wh/km;   
j is the index number of the considered phase;

k is the number of phases driven up to the end of the transition cycle n according to paragraph 3.2.4.4 of this Sub-Annex;

and

$$
\bf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O } _ { 2 } , \mathrm { { C D } , \mathrm { { a v g } , \mathrm { { p } } } } } } = \frac { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { c } } \left( \bf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O } _ { 2 } , \mathrm { { C D } , \mathrm { { p } , c } } } } \times \bf { d } _ { \mathrm { { p , c } } } \right) } { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { c } } \mathrm { { d } _ { \mathrm { { p , c } } } } }
$$

where:

$\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O } _ { 2 } , \mathrm { C D } , \mathrm { a v g } , \mathrm { p } }$ is the arithmetic average charge-depleting $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for the considered period p, $\mathrm { { g / k m } }$ ;   
$\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O } _ { 2 } , \mathrm { C D } , \mathrm { p } , \mathrm { c } }$ is the $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission determined according to paragraph 3.2.1. of Sub-Annex 7 of period $\mathfrak { p }$ in cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, $\mathrm { { g / k m } }$ ;   
${ \bf d } _ { \mathrm { p , c } }$ is the distance driven in the considered period $\mathfrak { p }$ of cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, km;   
c is the index number of the considered applicable WLTP test cycle;   
p is the index of the individual period within the applicable WLTP test cycle;   
nc is the number of applicable WLTP test cycles driven up to the end of the transition cycle n according to paragraph 3.2.4.4. of this Sub-Annex;

and

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { D C , C D , p } = \frac { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { c } } E C _ { D C , C D , p , c } \times d _ { p , c } } { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { c } } d _ { p , c } } }
$$

where:

ECDC,CD,p is the electric energy consumption of the considered period p based on the REESS depletion of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, Wh/km;   
ECDC,CD,p,c is the electric energy consumption of the considered period p of cycle c based on the REESS depletion of the charge-depleting Type 1 test according to paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex, Wh/km;   
${ \bf d } _ { \mathrm { p , c } }$ is the distance driven in the considered period p of cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, km;   
c is the index number of the considered applicable WLTP test cycle;   
p is the index of the individual period within the applicable WLTP test cycle;   
nc is the number of applicable WLTP test cycles driven up to the end of the transition cycle n according to paragraph 3.2.4.4. of this Sub-Annex.

The considered phase values shall be the low-phase, medium-phase, high-phase, extra high-phase, and the city driving cycle.

4.4.5. Actual charge-depleting range for OVC-HEVs

The actual charge-depleting range shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D A } } = \sum _ { \mathrm { c = 1 } } ^ { \mathrm { n - 1 } } \mathrm { d } _ { \mathrm { c } } + \left( \frac { \mathrm { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C S } } - \mathrm { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , n , c y c l e } } } { \mathrm { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , c S } } - \mathrm { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C D , a v g , n - 1 } } } \right) \times \mathrm { d } _ { \mathrm { n } }
$$

where:

<table><tr><td>RCDA</td><td>is the actual charge-depleting range, km;</td></tr><tr><td>Mco2.cs</td><td>isthe charge-sustaining COz massemission according to Table A8/5,step no.7,g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Mco2,n,cycle</td><td>is the COz mass emission of the applicable WLTP test cycle n of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Mc02,CD,avg,n-1</td><td>is the arithmetic average COz mass emission of the charge-depleting Type 1 test from the beginning up to and including the applicable WLTP test cycle (n-1), g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>dc</td><td>is the distance driven in the applicable WLTP test cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test,km;</td></tr><tr><td>dn</td><td>is the distance driven in the applicable WLTP test cycle n of the charge-depleting Type 1 test,km;</td></tr><tr><td>C</td><td>is the index number of the considered applicable WLTP test cycle;</td></tr><tr><td>n</td><td>is the number of applicable WLTP test cycles driven including the transition cycle according to paragraph 3.2.4.4.of this Sub-Annex;</td></tr></table>

and

$$
\bf M _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C D , a v g , n - 1 } } = \frac { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n - 1 } ( \bf M _ { \mathrm { C O 2 , C D , c } } \times d _ { c } ) } { \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n - 1 } d _ { c } }
$$

where:

MCO2,CD,avg,n–1 is the arithmetic average $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission of the charge-depleting Type 1 test from the beginning up to and including the applicable WLTP test cycle (n-1), g/km;

<table><tr><td colspan="3">VB</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>McO2.CD,c</td><td>is the COz mass emission determined according to paragraph 3.2.1.of Sub-Annex 7 of the applicable WLTP test cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>d</td><td>is the distance driven in the applicable WLTP test cycle c of the charge-depleting Type 1 test,km;</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>C</td><td>is the index number of the considered applicable WLTP test cycle;</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>n</td><td>is the number of applicable WLTP test cycles driven including the transition cycle according to paragraph 3.2.4.4 of this Sub-Annex;</td></tr><tr><td>4.5.</td><td colspan="2">Interpolation of individual vehicle values</td></tr><tr><td>4.5.1.</td><td colspan="2">Interpolation range for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs</td></tr></table>

The interpolation method shall only be used if the difference in charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission, $\operatorname { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 } , \mathrm { { C S } } } }$ , according to Table A8/5, step no. 8 between test vehicles $\mathrm { L }$ and $\mathrm { H }$ is between a minimum of $5 \mathrm { g / k m }$ and a maximum of 20 per cent plus $5 \ \mathrm { g / k m }$ of the charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission, $\operatorname { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 } , \mathrm { { C S } } } }$ , according to Table A8/5, step no. 8 for vehicle H, but at least $1 5 \ : \mathrm { g / k m }$ and not exceeding $2 0 \ \mathrm { g / k m }$ .

At the request of the manufacturer and with approval of the approval authority, the application of the interpolation method on individual vehicle values within a family may be extended if the maximum extrapolation is not more than $3 ~ \mathrm { g / k m }$ above the chargesustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission of vehicle H and/or is not more than $3 ~ \mathrm { g / k m }$ below the charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission of vehicle L. This extension is valid only within the absolute boundaries of the interpolation range specified in this paragraph.

The maximum absolute boundary of $2 0 ~ \mathrm { g / k m }$ charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission difference between vehicle L and vehicle $\mathrm { H }$ or 20 per cent of the charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for vehicle $\mathrm { H }$ , whichever is smaller, may be extended by $1 0 ~ \mathrm { g / k m }$ if a vehicle M is tested. Vehicle M is a vehicle within the interpolation family with a cycle energy demand within $\pm \nobreakspace 1 0 \nobreakspace$ per cent of the arithmetic average of vehicles L and H.

The linearity of charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for vehicle M shall be verified against the linear interpolated charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission between vehicle L and H.

The linearity criterion for vehicle M shall be considered fulfilled if the difference between the charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission of

▼B

vehicle $\mathbf { M }$ derived from the measurement and the interpolated charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission between vehicle $\mathrm { L }$ and $\mathrm { H }$ is below $1 \ \mathrm { g / k m }$ . If this difference is greater, the linearity criterion shall be considered to be fulfilled if this difference is $3 ~ \mathrm { g / k m }$ or 3 per cent of the interpolated charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for vehicle M, whichever is smaller.

If the linearity criterion is fulfilled, the interpolation method shall be applicable for all individual vehicles between vehicles $\mathrm { L }$ and $\mathrm { H }$ within the interpolation family.

If the linearity criterion is not fulfilled, the interpolation family shall be split into two sub-families for vehicles with a cycle energy demand between vehicles L and M, and vehicles with a cycle energy demand between vehicles M and H.

For vehicles with a cycle energy demand between that of vehicles L and M, each parameter of vehicle H necessary for the application of the interpolation method on individual OVC-HEV and NOVC-HEV values, shall be substituted by the corresponding parameter of vehicle M.

For vehicles with a cycle energy demand between that of vehicles M and $\mathrm { H } _ { \mathrm { \cdot } }$ , each parameter of vehicle L that is necessary for the application of the interpolation method on individual OVC-HEV and NOVC-HEV values shall be substituted by the corresponding parameter of vehicle M.

# 4.5.2. Calculation of energy demand per period

The energy demand $\operatorname { E } _ { \mathrm { k , p } }$ and distance driven ${ \mathrm { d } } _ { \mathrm { c , p } }$ per period p applicable for individual vehicles in the interpolation family shall be calculated according to the procedure in paragraph 5. of SubAnnex 7, for the sets $\mathrm { k }$ of road load coefficients and masses according to paragraph 3.2.3.2.3. of Sub-Annex 7.

4.5.3.

Calculation of the interpolation coefficient for individual vehicles Kind,p

The interpolation coefficient $\mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } }$ per period shall be calculated for each considered period $\mathfrak { p }$ using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } = { \frac { \mathrm { E } _ { 3 , \mathrm { p } } - \mathrm { E } _ { 1 , \mathrm { p } } } { \mathrm { E } _ { 2 , \mathrm { p } } - \mathrm { E } _ { 1 , \mathrm { p } } } }
$$

where:

Kind,p is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for period p;

E1,p

is the energy demand for the considered period for vehicle L in accordance with paragraph 5. of Sub-Annex 7, Ws;

<table><tr><td>E2,P</td><td>is the energy demand for the considered period for vehicle H in accordance with paragraph 5.of Sub-Annex 7,Ws;</td></tr><tr><td>3.P</td><td>is the energy demand for the considered period for the individual vehicle in accordance with paragraph 5.of Sub-Annex 7, Ws;</td></tr><tr><td>P</td><td>is the index of the individual period within the applicable testcycle.</td></tr></table>

# 4.5.4.

<table><tr><td colspan="2">In the case that the considered period p is the applicable WLTP test</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">cycle, Kind,p is named Kind-</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Interpolation of the COz mass emission for individual vehicles Individual charge-sustaining CO2 mass emission for OVC-HEVs</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">and NOVC-HEVs The charge-sustaining CO2 mass emission for an individual vehicle</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">shall be calculated using the following equation:</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">Mco2-ind,Cs,p = Mo2-LCs,p + Kind,d × (Mco2-H,Cs,p-Mco2-LCS.p)</td></tr><tr><td colspan="2">where:</td></tr><tr><td>Mco2-ind,CS.p</td><td>is the charge-sustaining COz mass emission for an individualvehicleoftheconsideredperiodp according to Table A8/5,step no. 9,g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Mc02-L.CS,p</td><td>is the charge-sustaining CO2 mass emission for vehicle L of the considered period p according to Table A8/5, step no. 8, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Mc02-H,CS,p</td><td>is the charge-sustaining COz mass emission for vehicle H of the considered period p according to Table A8/5, step no. 8, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kindd</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for period p;</td></tr><tr><td>p</td><td>is the index of the individual period within the applicable WLTP test cycle.</td></tr></table>

The considered periods shall be the low phase, medium phase, high phase, extra high phase, and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

Individual utility factor-weighted charge-depleting $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted charge-depleting $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 - i n d , C D } } = \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 - L , C D } } + \mathbf { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d } } \times \left( \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 - H , C D } } - \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { C O 2 - L , C D } } \right)
$$

where:

<table><tr><td></td><td>McO2-ind.CDis the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting CO2 mass emission for an individual vehicle,g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>MC02-L.CD</td><td>is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting CO2 mass emission for vehicle L,g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>MC02-H.CD</td><td>is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting CO2 mass emission for vehicle H, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kind</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle.</td></tr></table>

4.5.4.3.

Individual utility factor-weighted $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 - i n d } , w e i g h t e d } } = \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 - L , w e i g h t e d } } } + \mathbf { K } _ { \mathrm { { i n d } } } \times \left( \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 - H } , w e i g h t e d } } - \mathbf { M } _ { \mathrm { { C O 2 - L } , w e i g h t e d } } \right)
$$

where:

MCO2–ind,weighted is the utility factor-weighted $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for an individual vehicle, $\mathrm { { g / k m } }$ ;

<table><tr><td>McO2-H,weightedis the utility_factor-weighted CO2 mass emission</td><td>for vehicle H, g/km;</td></tr><tr><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td>Kind</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle.</td></tr></table>

# 4.5.5.

Interpolation of the fuel consumption for individual vehicles

4.5.5.1.

Individual charge-sustaining fuel consumption for OVC-HEVs and NOVC-HEVs

The charge-sustaining fuel consumption for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { F C _ { i n d , C S , p } = F C _ { L , C S , p } + K _ { i n d , p } \times ( F C _ { H , C S , p } - F C _ { L , C S , p } ) }
$$

where:

FCind,CS,p is the charge-sustaining fuel consumption for an individual vehicle of the considered period p according to Table ${ \mathrm { A } } 8 / 6 ,$ step no. 3, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
FCL,CS,p is the charge-sustaining fuel consumption for vehicle L of the considered period p according to Table A8/6, step no. 2, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
FCH,CS,p is the charge-sustaining fuel consumption for vehicle H of the considered period p according to Table A8/6, step no. 2, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
Kind,p is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for period p;   
p is the index of the individual period within the applicable WLTP test cycle.

The considered periods shall be the low phase, medium phase, high phase, extra high phase, and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

Individual utility factor-weighted charge depleting fuel consumption for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted charge-depleting fuel consumption for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { i n d , C D } } = \mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { L , C D } } + \mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d } } \times \left( \mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { H , C D } } - \mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { L , C D } } \right)
$$

<table><tr><td colspan="2">where:</td></tr><tr><td>FCind,CD</td><td>istheutility factor-weighted charge-depletingfuel consumption for an individual vehicle,l/100 km;</td></tr><tr><td>FCL.CD</td><td>istheutility factor-weighted_charge-depletingfuel consumption for vehicle L,l/100 km;</td></tr><tr><td>FCH.CD</td><td>isthe utility factor-weighted charge-depletingfuel consumption for vehicle H, l/100 km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kind</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle.</td></tr></table>

4.5.5.3. Individual utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for OVC-HEVs The utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

<table><tr><td colspan="2">FCind,weighted =FCL,weighted +Kind ×(FCH,weighted-FCL,weighted)</td></tr><tr><td>where:</td><td></td></tr><tr><td></td><td>FCind,weightedis the utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for an individual vehicle,l/10o0 km;</td></tr><tr><td>FCL,weighted</td><td>is the utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for vehicle L, 1/100 km;</td></tr><tr><td>FCH,weighted</td><td>is the utility factor-weighted fuel consumption for vehicle H, i/100 km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kind</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle.</td></tr></table>

# 4.5.6

Interpolation of electric energy consumption for individual vehicles

4.5.6.1. Individual utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { A C - i n d , C D } = E C _ { A C - L , C D } + K _ { i n d } \times ( E C _ { A C - H , C D } - E C _ { A C - L , C D } ) }
$$

where:

is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for an individual vehicle, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;

ECAC–L,CD is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for vehicle L, Wh/km;   
ECAC–H,CD is the utility factor-weighted charge-depleting electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for vehicle H, Wh/km;   
$\mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d } }$ is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle

4.5.6.2.

Individual utility factor-weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for OVC-HEVs

The utility factor-weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { A C - i n d , w e i g h t e d } = \mathrm { E C _ { A C - L , w e i g h t e d } + \mathrm { K } _ { i n d } \times ( \mathrm { E C _ { A C - H , w e i g h t e d } - E C _ { A C - L , w e i g h t e d } ) } } }
$$

where:

ECAC–ind,weighted is the utility factor weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for an individual vehicle, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
ECAC–L,weighted is the utility factor weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for vehicle L, $\mathrm { W h / k m }$ ;   
ECAC–H,weighted is the utility factor weighted electric energy consumption based on the recharged electric energy from the mains for vehicle H, Wh/km;   
Kind is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for the applicable WLTP test cycle.

4.5.6.3.

Individual electric energy consumption for OVC-HEVs and PEVs

The electric energy consumption for an individual vehicle according to paragraph 4.3.3. of this Sub-Annex in the case of OVC-HEVs and according to paragraph 4.3.4. of this Sub-Annex in the case of PEVs shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E C _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } = E C _ { L , p } + K _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } \times \left( E C _ { H , p } - E C _ { L , p } \right) }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E C } _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } }$ is the electric energy consumption for an individual vehicle for the considered period p, Wh/km;   
ECL,p is the electric energy consumption for vehicle L for the considered period p, Wh/km;   
ECH,p is the electric energy consumption for vehicle H for the considered period p, Wh/km;   
Kind,p is the interpolation coefficient for the considered individual vehicle for period p;   
p is the index of the individual period within the applicable test cycle.

The considered periods shall be the low phase, medium phase, high phase, extra high phase, the applicable WLTP city test cycle and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

Interpolation of electric ranges for individual vehicles

4.5.7.1.

Individual all-electric range for OVC-HEVs

If the following criterion

$$
| \frac { \mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { L } } } { \mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D A , L } } } - \frac { \mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { H } } } { \mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D A , H } } } | \leq 0 , 1
$$

where:

$\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { L } }$ : is the all-electric range of vehicle L for the applicable WLTP test cycle, km;

$\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { H } }$ : is the all-electric range of vehicle H for the applicable WLTP test cycle, km;

$\mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D A , L } }$ : is the actual charge-depleting range of vehicle L, km;

$\mathrm { R } _ { \mathrm { C D A , H } }$ : is the actual charge-depleting range of vehicle H, km;

is fulfilled, the all-electric range for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } = \mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { L , p } } + \mathrm { K } _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } \times \left( \mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { H , p } } - \mathrm { A E R } _ { \mathrm { L , p } } \right)
$$

where:

AERind,p is the all-electric range for an individual vehicle for the considered period p, km;

<table><tr><td>AERL,p</td><td>is the all-electric range for vehicle L for the considered period p, km;</td></tr><tr><td>AERH,p</td><td>is the all-electric range for vehicle H for the considered periodp,km</td></tr><tr><td>Kind,p</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for period p;</td></tr><tr><td>P</td><td>isthe index of the individual period within the applicable test cycle.</td></tr></table>

The considered periods shall be the applicable WLTP city test cycle and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

If the criterion defined in this paragraph is not fulfilled, the AER determined for vehicle $\mathrm { H }$ is applicable to all vehicles within the interpolation family.

4.5.7.2. Individual pure electric range for PEVs

The pure electric range for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { P E R _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } = \mathrm { P E R _ { \mathrm { L , p } } + K _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } \times ( \mathrm { P E R _ { H , p } - \mathrm { P E R _ { L , p } ) } } } }
$$

<table><tr><td>where:</td><td></td></tr><tr><td>PERind,p</td><td>is the pure electric range for an individual vehicle for the considered period p, km;</td></tr><tr><td>PERL,p</td><td>is the pure electric range for vehicle L for the considered period p,km;</td></tr><tr><td>PERH,p</td><td>is the pure electric range for vehicle H for the considered period p,km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kindp</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for period p;</td></tr><tr><td>P</td><td>isthe index of the individual period within the applicable test cycle.</td></tr></table>

The considered periods shall be the low phase, medium phase, high phase, extra high phase, the applicable WLTP city test cycle and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

# 4.5.7.3.

Individual equivalent all-electric range for OVC-HEVs

The equivalent all-electric range for an individual vehicle shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E A E R _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } = E A E R _ { \mathrm { L , p } } + K _ { \mathrm { i n d , p } } \times ( E A E R _ { \mathrm { H , p } } - E A E R _ { \mathrm { L , p } } ) }
$$

<table><tr><td colspan="2">where:</td></tr><tr><td>EAERind,p</td><td>is the equivalent all-electric range for an individual vehicle for the considered period p, km;</td></tr><tr><td>EAERLp</td><td>is the equivalent all-electric range for vehicle L for the considered period p, km;</td></tr><tr><td>EAERH,p</td><td>is the equivalent all-electric range for vehicle H for the considered period p, km;</td></tr><tr><td>Kind,p</td><td>is the interpolation coefficient for the considered indi- vidual vehicle for period p;</td></tr><tr><td>P</td><td>isthe index of the individual period within the applicable test cycle.</td></tr></table>

The considered periods shall be the low-phase, mid-phase, highphase, extra high-phase, applicable WLTP city test cycle and the applicable WLTP test cycle.

Sub-Annex 8

Appendix 2

# REESS energy change-based correction procedure

This Appendix describes the procedure to correct the charge-sustaining Type 1 test $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs, and the fuel consumption for NOVC-FCHVs as a function of the electric energy change of all REESSs.

1. General requirements   
1.1. Applicability of this Appendix   
1.1.1. The phase-specific fuel consumption for NOVC-FCHVs, and the $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs shall be corrected.

1.1.2. In the case that a correction of fuel consumption for NOVC-FCHVs or a correction of $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs measured over the whole cycle according to paragraph 1.1.3. or paragraph 1.1.4. of this Appendix is applied, paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex shall be used to calculate the charge-sustaining REESS energy change $\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { C S } }$ of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test. The considered period j used in paragraph 4.3. of this Sub-Annex is defined by the charge-sustaining Type 1 test.

1.1.3. The correction shall be applied if $\Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { C S } }$ is negative which corresponds to REESS discharging and the correction criterion c calculated in paragraph 1.2. of this Appendix is greater than the applicable threshold in accordance with Table $_ { \mathrm { A 8 . A p p 2 / 1 } }$ .

1.1.4. The correction may be omitted and uncorrected values may be used if:

(a) ΔEREESS,CS is positive which corresponds to REESS charging and the correction criterion c calculated in paragraph 1.2. of this Appendix is greater than the applicable threshold in accordance with Table $_ { \mathrm { A 8 . A p p 2 / 1 } }$ ;   
(b) The correction criterion c calculated in paragraph 1.2. of this Appendix is smaller than the applicable threshold in accordance with Table $_ { \mathrm { A 8 . A p p 2 / 1 } }$ ;   
(c) The manufacturer can prove to the approval authority by measurement that there is no relation between $\Delta \mathrm { b } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , C S } }$ and charge-sustaining $\mathrm { C O } _ { 2 }$ mass emission and $\Delta \mathrm { m } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S } , \mathrm { C S } }$ and fuel consumption respectively.

1.2.

The correction criterion c is the ratio between the absolute value of the REESS electric energy change ΔEREESS,CS and the fuel energy and shall be calculated as follows:

$$
\mathsf { c } = \frac { \left| \Delta \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { R E E S S , C S } } \right| } { \mathrm { E } _ { \mathrm { f u e l , C S } } }
$$

where:

ΔEREESS,CS is the charge-sustaining REESS energy change according to paragraph 1.1.2. of this Appendix, Wh;

is the charge-sustaining energy content of the consumed fuel in accordance with paragraph 1.2.1. of this Appendix in the case of NOVC-HEVs and OVCHEVs, and in accordance with paragraph 1.2.2. of this Appendix in the case of NOVC-FCHVs, Wh.

1.2.1. Charge-sustaining fuel energy for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs

The charge-sustaining energy content of the consumed fuel for NOVC-HEVs and OVC-HEVs shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
\mathrm { E _ { f u e l , C S } = 1 0 \times H V \times F C _ { C S , n b } \times d _ { C S } }
$$

where:

$\mathrm { E _ { f u e l , C S } }$ is the charge-sustaining energy content of the consumed fuel of the applicable WLTP test cycle of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test, Wh;   
HV is the heating value according to Table A6.App2/1, kWh/l;   
$\mathrm { F C } _ { \mathrm { C S } , \mathrm { n b } }$ is the non-balanced charge-sustaining fuel consumption of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test, not corrected for the energy balance, determined according to paragraph 6. of Sub-Annex 7, using the gaseous emission compound values according to Table A8/5, step no. 2, $1 / 1 0 0 \mathrm { k m }$ ;   
dCS is the distance driven over the corresponding applicable WLTP test cycle, km;   
10 conversion factor to Wh.

1.2.2. Charge-sustaining fuel energy for NOVC-FCHVs

The charge-sustaining energy content of the consumed fuel for NOVC-FCHVs shall be calculated using the following equation:

$$
{ \mathrm { E } } _ { \mathrm { f u e l , C S } } = { \frac { 1 } { 0 , 3 6 } } \times 1 2 1 \times { \mathrm { F C } } _ { \mathrm { C S , n b } } \times { \mathrm { d } } _ { \mathrm { C S } }
$$

Efuel,CS is the charge-sustaining energy content of the consumed fuel of the applicable WLTP test cycle of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test, Wh;   
121 is the lower heating value of hydrogen, $\mathrm { M J / k g }$ ;   
FCCS,nb is the non-balanced charge-sustaining fuel consumption of the charge-sustaining Type 1 test, not corrected for the energy balance, determined according to Table A8/7, step no.1, $\mathrm { k g / 1 0 0 k m }$ ;   
dCS is the distance driven over the corresponding applicable WLTP test cycle, km;   
$\frac { 1 } { 0 , 3 6 }$ conversion factor to Wh.
